name: Service Blueprint
description:
A service blueprint visualises how a service is produced across customer-facing interactions and the activities occurring behind them. It commonly aligns user actions, touchpoints, frontstage staff activity, backstage processes and supporting systems along a timeline.

The blueprint helps teams see dependencies between the experience people encounter and the organisational work required to deliver it.
whenToUse: Use service blueprints when designing or improving services involving multiple touchpoints, staff roles, systems or organisational processes.
steps: Define the service and scenario being mapped.
Identify the user's major actions over time.
Add visible touchpoints and frontstage interactions.
Map backstage activities supporting those interactions.
Add relevant systems, processes and supporting actors.
Examine how proposed changes affect both experience and delivery.
Revise the blueprint as the service develops.
lookOutFor: Do not confuse a service blueprint with a user journey: the blueprint includes organisational delivery as well as user experience.
Complex blueprints can become unreadable; define a clear scope.
Validate backstage processes with the people who actually perform them.

resources.citation: Shostack, G. L. (1984). “Designing Services That Deliver.” *Harvard Business Review*, 62(1), 133–139.
Bitner, M. J., Ostrom, A. L. & Morgan, F. N. (2008). “Service Blueprinting.” *California Management Review*, 50(3), 66–94.
